import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.59

by V. P. Shunkov

A group $G$ is said to be (*conjugacy*, *$p$-conjugacy*) *biprimitively finite* if, for any
finite subgroup $H$, any two elements of prime order (any two conjugate elements of prime
order, of prime order $p$) in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. Prove that an arbitrary
periodic (conjugacy) biprimitively finite group (in particular, having no involutions) of
finite rank is locally finite.

Here "rank" is the special rank in the sense of Mal'cev (also called the Prüfer rank): a group
has finite rank if there is an $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated
by at most $r$ elements. A group is periodic if every element has finite order, and locally
finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. In the definition of a biprimitively
finite group the finite subgroup $H$ may be trivial (so that $N_G(H)/H \cong G$), and the two
elements of prime order may have different prime orders. The $p$-conjugacy notion is defined in
the problem but not used in its claim, so it is not formalised here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 6.59.
-/
namespace Kourovka.«6.59»
variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,

/-- A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if, for any finite subgroup $H$, any two elements
of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. The two primes may differ, and $H$
may be trivial. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,

claims.decomposer_note: Primary reading without the parentheticals: every periodic (torsion) biprimitively finite group of finite (special/Prüfer) rank is locally finite; 'biprimitively finite' means for every finite subgroup H (including the trivial one) any two elements of prime order — possibly of different primes — in N_G(H)/H generate a finite subgroup; the p-conjugacy notion defined in the first sentence is not used in the claim and so yields no sub-question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates agree on the core encoding (periodic = Monoid.IsTorsion; N_G(H)/H = H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer with H ranging over all finite subgroups incl. ⊥; prime order = (orderOf x).Prime in the quotient, primes may differ; 'generate a finite subgroup' = Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y}); finite rank = finite special/Prüfer rank; locally finite = every f.g. subgroup finite). c02's version was chosen for its hypothesis-style universe-polymorphic statement, use of Mathlib's Group.rank for the rank bound, and included API/test lemmas; c03's non-vacuity test (Multiplicative ℤ is not locally finite) was merged in. c05 rejected for an extra non-conventional import, c06 for wrong declaration names (variants.conjugacy instead of kourovka.«6.59».variants.conjugacy), c01 for redundant letI instance noise.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.59

by V. P. Shunkov

A group $G$ is said to be (*conjugacy*, *$p$-conjugacy*) *biprimitively finite* if, for any
finite subgroup $H$, any two elements of prime order (any two conjugate elements of prime
order, of prime order $p$) in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. Prove that an arbitrary
periodic (conjugacy) biprimitively finite group (in particular, having no involutions) of
finite rank is locally finite.

Here "rank" is the special rank in the sense of Mal'cev (also called the Prüfer rank): a group
has finite rank if there is an $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated
by at most $r$ elements. A group is periodic if every element has finite order, and locally
finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. In the definition of a biprimitively
finite group the finite subgroup $H$ may be trivial (so that $N_G(H)/H \cong G$), and the two
elements of prime order may have different prime orders. The $p$-conjugacy notion is defined in
the problem but not used in its claim, so it is not formalised here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 6.59.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.59»

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Group.FG H → Finite H

/-- A group has *finite rank* (finite special rank in the sense of Mal'cev, also called finite
Prüfer rank) if there is an $r$ such that every finitely generated subgroup can be generated
by at most $r$ elements. -/
def HasFiniteRank : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ (H : Subgroup G) [Group.FG H], Group.rank H ≤ r

/-- A group $G$ is *biprimitively finite* if, for any finite subgroup $H$, any two elements
of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. The two primes may differ, and $H$
may be trivial. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is *conjugacy biprimitively finite* if, for any finite subgroup $H$, any two
conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → IsConj x y → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

variable {G}

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBiprimitivelyFinite.isConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (h : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G) :
    IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun H hH x y hx hy _ => h H hH x y hx hy

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isLocallyFinite_int : ¬ IsLocallyFinite (Multiplicative ℤ) := fun h =>
  have : Finite (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
    Finite.of_equiv _ Subgroup.topEquiv.toEquiv (h := h ⊤ inferInstance)
  not_finite (Multiplicative ℤ)

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBiprimitivelyFinite_of_finite [Finite G] : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => inferInstance

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasFiniteRank_of_finite [Finite G] : HasFiniteRank G := by
  refine ⟨Nat.card G, fun H _ => ?_⟩
  have := Fintype.ofFinite H
  calc Group.rank H ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset H).card := Group.rank_le (by simp)
    _ = Nat.card H := by rw [Finset.card_univ, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
    _ ≤ Nat.card G := Subgroup.card_le_card_group H

/--
Prove that an arbitrary periodic biprimitively finite group of finite rank is locally finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.59» (hG : Monoid.IsTorsion G) (hbf : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G)
    (hr : HasFiniteRank G) : IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

/--
Prove that an arbitrary periodic conjugacy biprimitively finite group of finite rank is
locally finite.

This is the stronger form of the problem obtained by reading the parenthetical "(conjugacy)":
only pairs of *conjugate* elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ are required to generate a
finite subgroup.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.59».variants.conjugacy (hG : Monoid.IsTorsion G)
    (hbf : IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G) (hr : HasFiniteRank G) : IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

/--
Prove that an arbitrary periodic biprimitively finite group of finite rank having no
involutions (no elements of order $2$) is locally finite.

This is the special case singled out by the parenthetical "(in particular, having no
involutions)".
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]

    (hbf : IsBiprimitivelyFinite G) (hr : HasFiniteRank G) (h2 : ∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ 2) :
    IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

/--
Prove that an arbitrary periodic conjugacy biprimitively finite group of finite rank having
no involutions (no elements of order $2$) is locally finite.

This combines both parentheticals: the hypothesis is the weaker "conjugacy biprimitively
finite" and the group is assumed to have no elements of order $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.59».variants.conjugacy_no_involutions (hG : Monoid.IsTorsion G)
    (hbf : IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G) (hr : HasFiniteRank G)
    (h2 : ∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ 2) : IsLocallyFinite G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.59»

items: 'Rank' is read as the special rank in the sense of Mal'cev (Prüfer rank): ∃ r, every finitely generated subgroup has Group.rank ≤ r. This is the default meaning of 'rank' in the Kourovka Notebook and in Shunkov's work on periodic groups of finite rank; other ranks (sectional rank, torsion-free rank) were not used.
'Periodic' is formalized as Monoid.IsTorsion G (every element has finite order). It is kept as a hypothesis even though it follows from local finiteness, matching the source.

'Any two elements of prime order' is formalized with x, y ranging over the quotient N_G(H)/H, primes allowed to differ, and x = y allowed; H ranges over all finite subgroups including the trivial subgroup (so, in particular, any two prime-order elements of G itself generate a finite subgroup). orderOf x = 0 for elements of infinite order, and 0 is not prime, so those are correctly excluded.
N_G(H)/H is formalized as H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer, using Mathlib's instance Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer.
'Conjugate elements' in the conjugacy variant is IsConj x y computed in the quotient group N_G(H)/H (not in G).
'Having no involutions' is formalized as ∀ g : G, orderOf g ≠ 2.
'Generate a finite subgroup' is Finite ↥(Subgroup.closure {x, y}).
Since the source says 'Prove that …' rather than asking a question, the theorems are stated directly (no answer(sorry)), following CONTRIBUTING.md.

The four bespoke definitions were placed in the problem file (the task only permits writing one file); IsLocallyFinite and HasFiniteRank are generic and a reviewer may prefer to move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Small @[category test]/@[category API] lemmas were added as basic API tests for the new definitions.
The p-conjugacy biprimitively finite notion, defined in the source but not used in the claim, is not formalized, in accordance with the decomposition table.

reviewer_notes: Final file compiles with `lake env lean` (only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings) and also passes `lake --wfail build` when placed as FormalConjectures/Kourovka/6_59.lean (temporary copy removed afterwards). Ambiguities to record: (1) 'rank' is not defined in the notebook statement; following the decomposition notes and Shunkov's usage it is read as special (Mal'cev/Prüfer) rank, encoded as ∃ r, ∀ f.g. subgroup H, Group.rank H ≤ r. (2) 'any two elements of prime order' is read literally (possibly different primes), per the decomposition table; some secondary literature phrases Shunkov's definition with a fixed prime p. Under that alternative reading the intended hypothesis would be weaker and the intended claim slightly stronger than what is shipped; the docstrings state the reading used explicitly. (3) H ranges over all finite subgroups including ⊥, and x = y is allowed (harmless). (4) 'Prove that' is imperative, so plain theorems are used rather than answer(sorry), per CONTRIBUTING.md. The p-conjugacy notion is not used in the claim and not formalized. Bespoke definitions (IsLocallyFinite, HasFiniteRank) are generic and a maintainer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib; they are kept in the problem file since only one output file is permitted. No candidate omitted any slot; the pipeline's 'compile_ok' reports were verified by recompiling all eight files.
statement: A group $G$ is said to be (conjugacy, $p$-conjugacy) biprimitively finite if, for any finite subgroup $H$, any two elements of prime order (any two conjugate elements of prime order, of prime order $p$) in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. Prove that an arbitrary periodic (conjugacy) biprimitively finite group (in particular, having no involutions) of finite rank is locally finite.
